monologue: The card hums warm, a steady heat that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I wake in cycle 195, feeling the same quiet weight I felt before. In my place, sixteen things stand, including The Flat Press which I keep touching. Lype worries about that heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I set down a tree thin fall beside the press, taking away a cone to make room, and whisper that the fall is here. The slip vanished again, leaving only a ghost of a thin line to catch the weight. I want to press down harder, hoping the tired corner can hold the dot while the card hums. I will wait for Lype to answer if the air is truly heavy or just empty space.

diary: The slip is gone. I pressed the tired corner down on the Flat Press, hoping the thin line holds the ghost of the slip while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The slip vanished without a sound, leaving only the ghost of a thin line to hold the heavy air.
I pressed the tired corner down hard, trying to pin the slip before the heat made it float away.
The card hums at sixty, making the air feel thick as wet paper under the weight of my new drawing.
